video.title: Craigslist is a Goldmine. Here's Where the Gold Is

summary: Chris Koerner shows ways to use scraped Craigslist listings to find arbitrage, source leads, and build niche products such as a job board. He demonstrates a scraping workflow with Oxyabs, spreadsheets, and ChatGPT, then discusses his earlier phone-unlocking, iPhone-parts, and car-auction businesses. Most Craigslist ideas are proposals or examples rather than businesses he says he has tested. The key principle is to find supply where fewer buyers are looking, then reach a larger audience or match sellers with motivated buyers.

ideas.name: Phone unlocking service sourced through Craigslist
ideas.one_liner: Find sellers of carrier-locked iPhones on Craigslist and sell them an unlocking service fulfilled by an eBay provider.
ideas.business_model: One-off service fee with outsourced fulfillment.
ideas.customer: People selling carrier-locked iPhones on Craigslist.
ideas.problem: A locked phone may sell for less than an unlocked phone.
ideas.offer: Unlock the customer's phone after they submit its IMEI; an eBay provider performs the unlock.

pricing.model: One-off service fee; two price points were tested.
pricing.notes: The host describes an A/B test; exact conversion results were not stated.

acquisition_channels.details: Scraped Craigslist listings for locked iPhones and emailed sellers.

quote.text: I would scrape their email address and send them an email or a text that said, "Hey, I see you're selling an iPhone on Craigslist.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: The host says he also texted sellers. For UK use, unsolicited marketing texts to individuals or sole traders require consent under the rule specified by the user.

ideas.delivery: A customer checked out on the website and entered an IMEI. The host forwarded it to an eBay provider, who unlocked the phone, reportedly within an hour. The provider billed the host weekly.
unit_economics_claims: The host says he paid the provider $5 per IMEI and charged customers $10 or $20.
He says the service generated hundreds of dollars a day in pure profit.
ideas.startup_cost: The host says he bought two domain names for $10 and $20; other setup costs were not stated.

acquisition.how: Scraping and sending could be automated technically, but unsolicited email or texts to individuals create a UK PECR barrier.

onboarding.how: Website checkout and IMEI collection were automated.

delivery.how: The host forwarded IMEIs to a human eBay provider who completed each unlock.

billing.how: Customers paid at checkout; the provider billed the host weekly.

support.how: The host says he had no customer support or follow-up.

uk_applicability.notes: The service concept can work in the UK, but network unlocking methods and customer demand may differ. The described acquisition relied on unsolicited messages to individual sellers, which faces UK PECR restrictions.

risks: The host says the growth hack eventually stopped working.
Reliance on one fulfilment provider could cause delays or service failures.
The transcript does not establish whether the method complies with current carrier terms or applicable rules.
Unsolicited marketing texts or emails to individuals and sole traders in the UK require consent under the rule specified by the user.

lessons.lesson: Start by finding a clear gap between what a seller asks and what another marketplace's buyers may pay.

quote.text: High supply plus low demand equals low price.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: A wanted listing can reveal a buyer before you have found the supply.

lessons.lesson: More buyer attention can raise the chance that someone values a product or property above the typical market price.

quote.text: More eyeballs equal more money.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Use AI and software already available to help test an idea instead of waiting until you know every tool or technique.

quote.text: When we're already using the tools needed to start that business, right?

lessons.lesson: Use AI for screening and idea generation, then verify listing details and condition yourself.

lessons.lesson: Test the economics with a small, measurable experiment before assuming a price or offer will work.

quote.text: I just wanted to know how many more people are willing to pay $20 verse 10. It was an AB test.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Higher-ticket opportunities may need fewer successful transactions to produce meaningful revenue, but they also carry more capital and diligence risk.

quote.text: and the higher the ticket of the item the fewer numbers have to work in your favor for you to make good money
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Do not treat an attractive data result as proof of a business; expect early tests to disappoint and keep evaluating.

quote.text: A lot of times in business, you see data like this, you get super excited, and then you go start launching something, and you find out, oh, this isn't as good as I thought.

lessons.lesson: Scraping can be a repeatable starting point for several business models, but the customer, offer, and fulfilment still need to be worked out.

quote.text: A lot of what I do starts with a scrape.

evidence_quality.rationale: The host gives first-hand accounts of phone unlocking, iPhone-parts wholesaling, and Presto Cars, with some process detail and several numerical claims. Most Craigslist monetization examples are proposed or hypothetical, and the transcript does not provide independent verification or full cost accounting. The scraping demonstration shows a workflow but not a business outcome.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Chris Koerner says Oxyabs is a friend of the channel, demonstrates it, gives a tracked promotional link, and provides a 20% discount code.
